newsitem.title: USA: Hibernia seeks to tap extra reservoir for more oil.
newsitem.headline: Hibernia seeks to tap extra reservoir for more oil.

text.p: Peak production from Canada's massive Hibernia oil project off Newfoundland could be extended by tapping into an adjacent reservoir called Avalon, the project's operating company chief said Monday.

The owners of the project have limited information about Avalon, but the reservoir is conservatively estimated to hold 2 billion barrels of oil in place, compared with 1.8 billion barrels in place in the Hibernia reservoir.
"We believe the Avalon contains significant upside," said Harvey Smith, president of Hibernia Management and Development Co Ltd.
The C$6.2 billion ($4.6 billion) Hibernia project is scheduled to start pumping oil in December.

Production is currently expected to plateau at 135,000 barrels per day in 1999 and continue at that level for about six years, with 515 million barrels of oil recoverable from Hibernia and 100 million barrels from Avalon.
The life of the project could also be extended by tapping marginal satellite fields linked into Hibernia facilities, Smith said at a National Ocean Industries Association meeting.
Production from the satellite fields could take advantage of excess capacity on the Hibernia platform, which was designed to handle 150,000 bpd, he said.

The partners in Hibernia are Petro-Canada, with 20 percent, Mobil Corp unit Mobil Oil Canada Ltd, with 33.125 percent, Chevron Corp unit Chevron Canada Resources Ltd, with 26.875 percent, Murphy Oil Corp's Murphy Atlantic Offshore Oil Co Ltd, with 6.5 percent, the government of Canada's Canada Hibernia Holding Corp with 8.5 percent and Norsk Hydro A/S with five percent.
